title: Spec answers by option label; piped answers refused
lead: `ork run` and `ork wave start` refuse to read spec answers from standard input when it is not a terminal: they print every open question with its answer address, start nothing and exit 3. `--answer KEY=LABEL` picks the option whose label is LABEL, and a held batch prints each unanswered question in full, not only its key.
findings_note: 2026-11-17: the orchestrator ran `printf '1\n1\n' | ork run ...` with stock answers; the spec check had asked new questions, so the pipe answered questions the owner never saw. `askSpecQuestions` reads stdin whether or not it is a terminal (`internal/cli/wave.go:950-990`). S312 already gives `--answer KEY=N` and holds on any unanswered key (`internal/cli/wave.go:641-657,842-906`), but a label is taken as free text and the hold names only the keys.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner rule (2026-11-17): regular deterministic steps are code. What already exists (S312, done): `--questions`, repeatable `--answer KEY=N` or `KEY=text`, `#N` for a keyless question, and a hold with exit 3 when a key is missing (`internal/cli/wave.go:641-657`). What is still open:

- Piped input: `askSpecQuestions` (`internal/cli/wave.go:950-990`) reads numbers from any reader, so `printf '1\n1\n' | ork run P ID` answers whatever questions come first, including new ones. This session that happened (findings above). The terminal test already exists for spec drafts (`internal/cli/specdraft.go:35-50`, `App.Terminal` at `internal/cli/cli.go:279`).
- Labels: `--answer cache.store=memory` records the free text `memory`, not the option `memory: rebuilt at each start` (`internal/cli/wave.go:885-894` maps only numbers). A number is positional within the options and can pick the wrong option when the options change between the check and the answer; a label cannot.
- Held output: `held: unanswered spec questions: KEY, ...` (`internal/cli/wave.go:650`) names a new question's key but not its text, so the orchestrator cannot put it to the owner without `--questions` again.

Owner decisions (2026-11-17): `--answer` matches an option label trimmed and case-insensitive, a number still picks by position, other text is free text; standard input that is not a terminal is refused with exit 3; a keyless question stays `#N` [cli.spec-answers, adj 452].

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Fixture: `specCheckTwoQuestions` (`internal/cli/wave_test.go:357-359`): S1 has `cache.store` (options `file`, `memory`) and a keyless `What flag?` (options `short`, `long`).

- `TestRunRefusesPipedSpecAnswers` (`internal/cli/run_test.go`): `App{Input: "1\n1\ny\n", Terminal: func() bool { return false }}`, `ork run p S1`. Expected: exit 3, no `spec.answer` and no `run.start` call, stdout contains `[S1 1/2] Which store?`, `Decision key: cache.store`, `[S1 2/2] What flag?`, `Answer as: #2`, and the line `held: S1: standard input is not a terminal; answer each question with --answer KEY=LABEL`. Red: today the pipe answers both questions and the run starts.
- `TestWaveStartRefusesPipedSpecAnswers` (`internal/cli/wave_test.go`): `ork wave start p S1 S2 --yes` with the same non-terminal input: as for an incomplete `--answer` batch (`internal/cli/wave.go:649-657`), nothing starts, S2 included, and the exit is 3. Red: today S1's questions are answered from the pipe and both start.
- `TestBatchAnswerByLabel` (`internal/cli/spec_questions_test.go`): `--answer cache.store=memory --answer '#2=long' --yes`. Expected `spec.answer` answers `["memory: rebuilt at each start", "long: --extra"]`, run starts, exit 0. Red: today the answers recorded are `memory` and `long` as free text.
- `TestBatchAnswerLabelIgnoresCase`: `--answer cache.store=Memory` records `memory: rebuilt at each start`. Red as above.
- `TestBatchHeldPrintsTheUnansweredQuestions`: `--answer cache.store=file --yes` only. Expected exit 3, no `spec.answer` call, stdout contains `held: unanswered spec questions: #2`, then `[S1 2/2] What flag?`, `  1. short: -x (recommended)`, `  2. long: --extra` and `  Answer as: #2`; it does not print `[S1 1/2]`. Red: today only the held line is printed.
- Existing `TestRunAsksSpecQuestionsOnStdinThenStarts` (`internal/cli/run_test.go:884`) stays green: with `Input` set and no `Terminal`, `terminal()` returns true (`internal/cli/specdraft.go:39-41`).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Red tests above.
2. In `specCheck`, before the loop that calls `askSpecQuestions`: when `flags.answers` is empty, `a.terminal()` is false and any item has open questions, print each question with `printSpecQuestion(..., false, address)`, print the held line per item, read nothing, start nothing and return `ExitWaitQuestion` (3), as the incomplete-batch branch does.
3. In `mapAnswers`: after the number check, a value equal (case-insensitive, trimmed) to one option's label records `Label: Summary`. Any other text stays free text.
4. In the held-batch branch, print each unanswered question with `printSpecQuestion` after the held line.
5. Docs: `docs/guide.md` and `docs/design.md` (spec questions), the usage text. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet under `## Unreleased`.
6. UI slice: UI pass (r14), since `internal/cli` output changes.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- 'printf '1\n1\n' | ork run P ID' with open spec questions starts nothing, records nothing, prints every question with its answer address and exits 3.
- 'ork run P ID --answer KEY=LABEL ... --yes' records the option with that label.
- A batch that leaves a question out exits 3 and prints that question's full text and options.
- An interactive terminal prompt works as before.

Commands:
- `go -C /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork test ./internal/cli -run 'Piped|Batch|SpecQuestions'` exits 0.
- `go -C /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork vet ./...` exits 0.
- `go -C /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork test ./...` exits 0.
- `gofmt -l /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork` prints nothing.
- `slicer check --root /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork` and `adj lint --root /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork` exit 0.
